title: Face conservation in a categorical localization of a cocartesian three-horn
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns, quasicategories and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $H=\Lambda^3_2\subseteq\Delta^3$. Let $r:E\to H$ be an inner fibration, and suppose that every vertex of $E$ over $1$ is the source of an $r$-cocartesian edge over $1\to2$, with cocartesian understood by the outer-horn lifting condition over the arbitrary base $H$. Let $T$ be a small quasicategory, let $t:T\to\Delta^3$ be a simplicial map, and let $w:E\hookrightarrow T$ be a monomorphism and categorical equivalence with $tw=\iota r$, where $\iota:H\hookrightarrow\Delta^3$ is the inclusion. For each nonempty subset $J\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$ contained in at least one of $\{0,1,2\}$, $\{0,2,3\}$, $\{1,2,3\}$, let $\Delta^J\subseteq H$ be the face with ordered vertex set $J$, and put $E_J=E\times_H\Delta^J$ and $T_J=T\times_{\Delta^3}\Delta^J$. Then the induced map $w_J:E_J\to T_J$ is a categorical equivalence. No isomorphism of these face inverse images is asserted, and no preservation of cocartesian edges by $w$ is assumed.

source.place: Agent-formulated face-localization comparison for the repair of Lemma 3.1.2.4, printed pp.330-332. The printed K2 argument does not establish this comparison; this node is an unsplit supporting assertion, not an invocation of Lemma 3.1.2.4 or of the relative-completion nodes depending on it. Archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag supplies this quasicategorical comparison.

proof.text: For a face $J$ of $H$, every inner-horn lifting problem in $E_J$ lies over a simplex of $\Delta^J$; the horn filler in $E$ supplied by $r$ remains over that simplex. Thus $E_J$ is a quasicategory. The inverse image $T_J$ is the full simplicial subset of $T$ on vertices labelled by $J$: a simplex of $\Delta^3$ is determined by its ordered vertices. An inner filler in $T$ with those vertices therefore lies in $T_J$, so $T_J$ is also a quasicategory. The same vertex argument shows that, whenever $J\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $E_J$ is full in $E_F$. In particular right mapping spaces between vertices in $E_J$ are unchanged in $E_F$; those between vertices in $T_J$ are unchanged in $T$. This follows directly from the pinched mapping-simplex definition, whose vertices are its two endpoints. Set $A_i=\mathfrak C[E_i]$ and $M_{ij}(u,v)=\mathfrak C[E_{ij}](u,v)$, with their composition actions.

proof.text: Fix $u\in E_1$ and choose an $r$-cocartesian edge $e:u\to u_2$ over $1\to2$. It remains cocartesian for $E_{123}\to\Delta^{123}$: every relevant outer-horn lifting problem there is one for $r$, and its filler stays over the given simplex of $123$. This map is an inner fibration between quasicategories by Step 1. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. For $v\in E_2$ and $z\in E_3$, the two bottom mapping spaces in its square are points. Hence precomposition gives equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{E_2}(u_2,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{E_{12}}(u,v)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{23}}(u_2,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{E_{13}}(u,z)$. Step 1 justifies replacing the ambient face $123$ by these smaller faces. The natural mapping comparisons of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] and [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], including compatibility with composition, give objectwise weak equivalences of the enriched modules $A_2(u_2,-)\xrightarrow{e^*}M_{12}(u,-)$ and of spaces $M_{23}(u_2,z)\xrightarrow{e^*}M_{13}(u,z)$. No edge of $T$ is asserted cocartesian.

proof.text:
Consider the derived composition augmentation in face $123$,
$$k_{u,z}:M_{12}(u,-)\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbb L}M_{23}(-,z)\longrightarrow M_{13}(u,z).$$
The target is identified with the triangle-face mapping module through the natural full-face weak equivalence of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]; the augmentation is a map of derived modules, with no strict retraction asserted. By [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda], replacing its first module using Step 2 is an equivalence, and the action augmentation $A_2(u_2,-)\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbb L}M_{23}(-,z)\to M_{23}(u_2,z)$ is an equivalence. The square with this augmentation on top, $k_{u,z}$ on the bottom, and precomposition by $e$ on both vertical sides commutes: both composites compose the same string $u\xrightarrow e u_2\to v\to z$, using the specified enriched composition and bar augmentation. The right side is an equivalence by Step 2. Two-out-of-three gives that $k_{u,z}$ is an equivalence for every $u,z$. The maps $k_{u,z}$ themselves form the enriched composition pairing and hence are natural in $u,z$. The chosen lifts were used only to test them objectwise; no functorial choice of lifts is needed.

proof.text: For $x\in E_0$, $z\in E_3$, use the spaces $P,R,D$ of [lem-coef-directed-three-face-mapping-pushout] with $K=E$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 1. Its map $R(x,z)\to P(x,z)$ is the derived tensor of $M_{01}(x,-)$ with the composition pairing $k_{-,z}$ of Step 3. Fubini and invariance in [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda] therefore make $R(x,z)\to P(x,z)$ an equivalence. The other map $R\to D$ is completely specified: first compose $M_{01}\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbb L}M_{12}\to M_{02}$ in face $012$, then compose $M_{02}\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbb L}M_{23}\to M_{03}$ in face $023$. This is exactly the gluing span, not an assumption that a triangle with vertices $013$ was already in $E$.

proof.text: The gluing formula now reads $\mathfrak C[E](x,z)\simeq P(x,z)\amalg^h_{R(x,z)}D(x,z)$ with $R\to P$ an equivalence. Thus $D(x,z)\to\mathfrak C[E](x,z)$ is a weak equivalence: mapping this pushout to any space $V$ gives $\operatorname{Map}(P,V)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(R,V)}\operatorname{Map}(D,V)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(D,V)$. The identification of the map from $D$ with the actual inclusion is part of [lem-coef-directed-three-face-mapping-pushout]. The same node gives the inclusion comparisons for every pair $i\leq j$ other than $(0,3)$. Consequently, for every allowed face $J$ and vertices $a,b$ of $E_J$, the actual map $\mathfrak C[E_J](a,b)\to\mathfrak C[E](a,b)$ is a weak equivalence. For $(0,3)$ this uses the face $03$ calculation and the full-face mapping comparison of Step 1, via the natural pinched comparisons. For $i>j$ both mapping sets are empty, since their maps to $\mathfrak C[\Delta^3]$ would otherwise give a backward arrow. These cases exhaust the labels.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection], $\mathfrak C[w]:\mathfrak C[E]\to\mathfrak C[T]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. In particular it is a weak equivalence on each mapping simplicial set and essentially surjective on component categories. For vertices $a,b$ of $E_J$, Step 5 makes the composite $\mathfrak C[E_J](a,b)\to\mathfrak C[T](wa,wb)$ a weak equivalence. The map $\mathfrak C[T_J](wa,wb)\to\mathfrak C[T](wa,wb)$ is also a weak equivalence: right mapping spaces are identical by Step 1, and the two natural weak equivalences in [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] identify their $Q$-realizations with the displayed rigidified mapping sets. The commuting square for the actual inclusions and $w_J$, followed by two-out-of-three, proves that $\mathfrak C[w_J]$ is a weak equivalence on all mapping sets.

proof.text: Let $y$ be a vertex of $T_J$ with label $j$. Essential surjectivity of $\mathfrak C[w]$ on component categories supplies a vertex $x$ of $E$ and an isomorphism from $wx$ to $y$ in $\pi_0\mathfrak C[T]$. The functor $\pi_0\mathfrak C[T]\to\pi_0\mathfrak C[\Delta^3]=[3]$ sends this to an isomorphism in the ordered category $[3]$, so $x$ has label $j$ and belongs to $E_J$. By Step 6's full mapping comparison for $T_J\subseteq T$, both the isomorphism and its inverse lift to $\pi_0\mathfrak C[T_J]$. Their inverse equations hold there by injectivity on the same endomorphism sets. Hence $y$ is isomorphic to $w_Jx$ in $\pi_0\mathfrak C[T_J]$. This also covers a singleton $J$; if $E_J$ is empty the argument forces $T_J$ empty. Thus $\mathfrak C[w_J]$ is essentially surjective.

source.place: Agent mapping-space repair of the face comparison motivating HA Lemma 3.1.2.4, pp.330-332; not the printed K2 argument.

proof.text: The Dwyer--Kan criterion consists of weak equivalences on all mapping sets and essential surjectivity on the component category. Steps 6 and 7 give exactly these two properties for $\mathfrak C[w_J]$. Apply [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection] to $w_J:E_J\to T_J$ to conclude that it is a categorical equivalence. Every nonempty $J$ in the item is a face of $H$, so this proves all requested comparisons.
